Leave the clams in salted water for 30 minutes so they release their sand.
Salt the hake. In a wide pan, gently brown the chopped garlic in the oil.
Add the flour, stir for 1 minute and pour in the wine; let it reduce for 2 minutes.
Pour in the stock little by little, shaking the pan until the sauce thickens a bit.
Add the hake and clams, cover and cook for 5–6 minutes, shaking the pan now and then.
Sprinkle with chopped parsley and serve straight away.
The cod must be desalted: 48 hours in cold water in the fridge, changing the water 3 times a day.
Soak the choricero peppers in warm water for 1 hour and scrape out the flesh with a spoon.
Gently soften the chopped onion and garlic in the oil for 20 minutes.
Add the pepper flesh and the tomato, cook for 15 minutes and blend the sauce.
Place the cod skin side up in a pan, cover with the sauce and simmer for 10 minutes. Taste before salting: the cod is already salty.
Preheat the oven to 200 °C.
Slice the potatoes thinly, put them on a tray with half the oil and salt, and bake for 20 minutes.
Lay the seasoned salmon and lemon slices on top, and drizzle with the rest of the oil and the juice of half a lemon.
Bake for another 12–15 minutes, until the salmon is juicy inside.
Serve with more lemon to taste.
Preheat the oven to 220 °C. Gut the bream but don’t scale them.
Mix the coarse salt with a little water until it feels like wet sand.
Spread a layer of salt on a tray, lay the fish on top with a few lemon slices inside, and cover them completely with the rest.
Bake for 20–25 minutes.
Break the salt crust, remove the skin and serve the fillets with a drizzle of oil.
Preheat the oven to 200 °C. Ask the fishmonger to butterfly the sea bass.
Lay them open on a tray skin side down, salt them and drizzle with a little oil.
Bake for 12–15 minutes depending on size.
Meanwhile, brown the sliced garlic and the chilli in the rest of the oil. Off the heat, add the vinegar.
Pour the garlic oil over the fish and serve with lemon.
Gut the sardines and rinse them in cold water. Dry them well.
Heat the griddle until very hot with a little oil.
Sprinkle them with coarse salt and cook for 2–3 minutes on each side.
Serve with chopped parsley, a drizzle of oil and lemon.
Clean the anchovies, removing the heads and guts. Rinse and dry them well.
Salt them and coat in flour, shaking off the excess.
Fry in plenty of very hot oil, in small batches, for 1–2 minutes until golden.
Drain on kitchen paper and serve with lemon.
Clean the squid and cut into rings. Dry them well and salt them.
Coat in flour and then in beaten egg.
Fry in batches in plenty of very hot oil until golden.
Drain on kitchen paper and serve straight away with lemon.
Clean the cuttlefish and cut into large pieces. Dry well.
For the aioli: put the egg, 1 garlic clove, salt and the 120 ml of oil in the blender jug. Blend without moving until it thickens, then move the blender up and down.
Heat the griddle with a little oil and cook the cuttlefish for 3–4 minutes on each side.
At the end, add the other garlic clove and the parsley, chopped, with a drizzle of oil.
Serve with the aioli and lemon.
If the octopus is fresh, freeze it for at least 2 days first so it turns out tender (or buy it already cooked).
Bring a large pot of water to the boil. «Scare» the octopus: dip it in and out three times, then leave it in.
Cook for about 40 minutes, until a skewer goes in easily. Let it rest in the water for 10 minutes.
In the same water, cook the peeled, sliced potatoes for about 20 minutes.
Cut the octopus with scissors over the potatoes and finish with coarse salt, paprika and oil.
Clean the mussels, scraping the shells and pulling off the beards. Throw away any that are open.
Put the wine, bay leaf and a few lemon slices in a pot, and add the mussels.
Cover and cook over high heat for 4–5 minutes, shaking the pot, until they open.
Throw away any that haven’t opened and serve with lemon.
Chop the onion, pepper and garlic and soften them in the oil for 10 minutes in a pan.
Add the tomato and cook for 5 more minutes.
Add the peeled potatoes, «cracked» (break off the last cut so they release starch), and stir for 2 minutes.
Cover with the hot stock and simmer for 20–25 minutes, until the potatoes are tender.
Turn off the heat, add the diced tuna with salt and leave covered for 5 minutes: it cooks in the residual heat.
Salt the monkfish, coat in flour and brown it in the oil. Set aside.
In the same oil fry the almonds, garlic and bread until golden. Blend them with a little stock.
Soften the chopped onion for 10 minutes, add the wine and let it reduce.
Add the almond paste, the saffron and the rest of the stock, and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the monkfish and cook for 6–8 minutes over low heat.
Slice the onions thinly and cook them slowly in the oil with the garlic and bay leaf for 25 minutes, until very soft.
Add the wine and let the alcohol evaporate.
Cut the tuna into chunks, season and add it to the onion.
Cook for just 3–4 minutes, turning it: if overcooked, it gets dry.
Clean the trout, dry them and salt the inside.
Put a slice of ham inside each trout.
Coat in flour and fry in the oil for 4–5 minutes on each side.
Serve with lemon.
Chop the garlic and parsley and mix them with the oil and a little lemon juice.
Salt the swordfish steaks.
Cook them on a very hot griddle for 2–3 minutes on each side.
Serve with the garlic and parsley dressing on top.
Preheat the oven to 200 °C.
Thinly slice the potatoes, onion and pepper, put them on a tray with half the oil and salt, and bake for 20 minutes.
Lay the cleaned, salted mackerel on top, and drizzle with the wine and the rest of the oil.
Bake for another 15 minutes.
The cod must be desalted (48 hours in cold water, changing it 3 times a day). Dry it well.
Gently brown the sliced garlic and the chilli in the oil. Take them out.
Let the oil cool a little and add the cod skin side up. Cook over very low heat for 5 minutes on each side.
Remove the cod and swirl the pan in circles (or whisk with a sieve) until the gelatine from the cod emulsifies the oil into a thick sauce.
Put the cod back, cover with the sauce and garnish with the garlic and chilli.
Salt the cleaned sole and dry them well.
Brush the griddle with oil and, when very hot, add the sole.
Cook for 3–4 minutes on each side depending on thickness.
Serve with lemon and a lettuce salad dressed with oil, vinegar and salt.
Steam the mussels open and set aside. Peel the prawns.
In a pan, fry the chopped onion and garlic in the oil for 10 minutes. Add the tomato and cook for 10 more minutes.
Add the wine, let it reduce and pour in the stock with the saffron and the chopped almonds.
Add the squid rings and cook for 10 minutes.
Add the monkfish and hake in pieces and the prawns, and cook for 5–6 minutes. Add the mussels at the end.
Mix the meat with the egg, the breadcrumbs soaked in the milk, 1 garlic clove and the parsley, chopped, and salt. Shape into balls.
Coat in flour and brown in the oil. Set aside.
In that oil, soften the chopped onion, the other garlic clove and the carrot for 15 minutes.
Add the tomato and wine, let it reduce and pour in the stock. Cook for 10 minutes and blend the sauce.
Put the meatballs back in the sauce and simmer for 15 minutes.
Cut the potatoes into sticks and fry in plenty of oil until golden. Drain and salt.
Fry the Padrón peppers in a little oil until wrinkled and sprinkle with coarse salt.
Salt the loin steaks and cook on a very hot griddle for 1–2 minutes on each side.
Serve the pork with the peppers and chips.
Salt the steaks and coat them in beaten egg and then breadcrumbs, pressing well.
Fry in hot oil for 1–2 minutes on each side and drain on paper.
Fry the potatoes cut into sticks and salt them.
Serve with lemon.
Season the meat, divide into 4 balls and flatten them to 1.5 cm thick.
Cook in a hot pan or griddle with a few drops of oil, 3–4 minutes on each side.
In the last minute, put the cheese on top so it melts.
Lightly toast the buns and build the burgers with lettuce, tomato and sliced onion.
Salt the diced beef, coat in flour and brown it in the oil in a pot. Set aside.
In the same oil soften the chopped onion, garlic and carrot for 10 minutes.
Return the meat, add the wine and let the alcohol evaporate.
Cover with the stock, add the bay leaf and simmer covered for 1½ hours (or 30 minutes in a pressure cooker).
Add the potatoes in chunks and the peas, and cook for 20 more minutes.
Trim the fat off the pork cheeks, season, coat in flour and brown in the oil. Set aside.
Soften the chopped onion, carrot and garlic for 15 minutes.
Add the cheeks and the wine, and let it reduce for 5 minutes.
Cover with the stock and simmer covered over very low heat for 2½ hours (or 40 minutes in a pressure cooker), until they fall apart.
Blend the sauce. Serve with boiled or mashed potatoes.
Preheat the oven to 180 °C.
Mix the oil, chopped garlic, paprika, lemon juice and salt, and rub it well over the ribs.
Put the sliced potatoes on the tray with the ribs on top. Drizzle with the wine.
Bake for 1 hour, turning halfway. Raise to 220 °C for the last 10 minutes to brown them.
Boil the peeled potatoes in salted water for 20 minutes.
Cut the tenderloin into medallions, season and brown in the oil for 2 minutes on each side. Set aside.
In the same pan pour in the wine, let it reduce and add the cream and mustard.
Cook the sauce for 3 minutes, return the meat and cook for 2 more minutes.
Serve with the potatoes.
Slice the potatoes and cut the peppers into strips, and fry them over medium heat until tender and golden. Drain and salt.
Heat a griddle until very hot without oil: the secreto already has its own fat.
Cook the secreto for 3–4 minutes on each side, cut into strips and sprinkle with coarse salt.
Serve with the potatoes and peppers.
Season the chops and brown them in the oil for 3–4 minutes on each side. Set aside.
In the same pan add the butter, the thinly sliced onion and the apple in wedges, and cook for 10 minutes.
Add the wine and let it reduce.
Return the chops, cover and cook for 3 more minutes.
Salt the rabbit and brown it well in the oil over medium-high heat, about 15 minutes.
Add the whole garlic cloves in their skins, lightly crushed, and the bay leaf, and cook for 5 minutes.
Pour in the wine, cover and cook over low heat for 20 minutes, until tender.
Uncover, let the sauce reduce and finish with chopped parsley.
Preheat the oven to 190 °C. Cut the tops off the peppers and remove the seeds.
Soften the chopped onion and garlic in the oil for 10 minutes. Add the meat and salt, and cook until no longer pink.
Mix with half the tomato sauce and stuff the peppers.
Cover with the rest of the tomato and the cheese, put their «lids» on and bake for 40 minutes.
Brown the diced meat in the oil and set aside.
Soften the chopped onion, carrot and garlic for 10 minutes.
Return the meat, add the wine, let it reduce and add the tomato and stock.
Simmer covered for 2 hours (or 35 minutes in a pressure cooker), until the meat falls apart.
For the mash, boil the potatoes for 20 minutes, drain and mash with the hot milk, butter and salt. Serve the ragù over the mash.
Salt the chicken and brown it well in the oil over medium heat, about 20 minutes, turning it.
Add the garlic cloves in their skins, lightly crushed, and cook for 5 more minutes.
Pour in the wine and let it reduce over high heat.
Cover and cook for 10 minutes over low heat. Finish with chopped parsley.
Preheat the oven to 200 °C.
Put the sliced potatoes and onions on a tray with salt and half the oil.
Season the chicken inside and out, put the halved lemon and the garlic inside, and rub it with the rest of the oil.
Place it on the potatoes, drizzle with the wine and roast for 1¼ hours, turning halfway and basting with its juices.
Cut the chicken breasts into thin fillets and salt them.
Cook them on a hot griddle with a few drops of oil for 2–3 minutes on each side.
Make the salad with the lettuce, tomato and onion, and dress it with oil, vinegar and salt.
Serve the chicken with the salad.
Boil the rice in salted water for 18 minutes and drain.
Soften the chopped onion in the oil for 8 minutes.
Add the diced chicken and salt, and brown it. Add the curry and stir for 1 minute.
Pour in the coconut milk and simmer for 10 minutes until it thickens.
Serve with the rice.
Boil the eggs for 10 minutes and separate the yolks from the whites.
Salt the chicken, coat in flour and brown it in the oil. Set aside.
In the same oil fry the garlic and almonds and set aside. Soften the chopped onion for 10 minutes.
Return the chicken, add the wine, let it reduce and cover with the stock. Cook for 30 minutes.
Crush the almonds, garlic, yolks and saffron with a little stock, add to the pan and cook for 5 minutes. Serve with the chopped egg white on top.
Preheat the oven to 200 °C.
Put the sliced potatoes and onion on a tray with salt and a little oil.
Rub the thighs with the rest of the oil, the lemon juice, paprika and salt, and place them on top.
Bake for 45–50 minutes, turning halfway, until the skin is golden.
Cut the turkey into strips, season and brown in the oil. Set aside.
In the same pan soften the chopped onion for 5 minutes and add the sliced mushrooms. Cook until their water evaporates and they brown.
Return the turkey, add the cream and cook for 5 minutes.
Goes well with rice or potatoes.
Cut the chicken, peppers and onion into strips.
Stir-fry the vegetables in the oil over high heat for 5 minutes and set aside.
Stir-fry the chicken with salt, cumin and paprika until golden, and mix with the vegetables.
Warm the tortillas and fill them with the chicken, vegetables and sliced avocado with a few drops of lemon.
Salt the chicken and brown it in the oil. Set aside.
Soften the onion, garlic and peppers in strips for 15 minutes. Add the diced ham.
Add the tomato and cook for 10 minutes.
Return the chicken, pour in the wine and simmer covered for 25 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 210 °C.
Mix the oil, chopped garlic, lemon juice, paprika and salt, and coat the wings.
Put the potato wedges on a tray with the wings on top.
Bake for 40 minutes, turning halfway, until crispy.
Boil the rice in salted water for 18 minutes.
Cut the chicken into strips, salt it, coat in flour and brown in the oil.
Add the sliced garlic, the juice and zest of the lemons, and the stock.
Cook for 5 minutes, until the sauce thickens. Serve with the rice.
Trim the artichokes and boil them for 15 minutes in salted water. Separately boil the beans, carrot and peas for 10 minutes and keep a glass of the water.
Soften the chopped onion and garlic in the oil. Add the diced ham.
Add the flour, stir and pour in the glass of vegetable cooking water.
Add all the drained vegetables and cook for 5 minutes so the flavours blend.
Cut all the vegetables into small dice.
Soften the onion and peppers in the oil for 10 minutes.
Add the aubergine and courgette and cook for 15 more minutes.
Add the tomato, sugar and salt, and simmer for 15 minutes.
Serve with a fried or griddled egg on top.
Peel and chop the pumpkin, potato and carrot. Slice the leek.
Sweat the leek in the oil for 5 minutes.
Add the rest of the vegetables, cover with the stock and cook for 25 minutes.
Blend until smooth and season with salt.
Slice the leek and sweat it in the oil for 5 minutes.
Add the courgette and potato in chunks and stir for 2 minutes.
Cover with the stock and cook for 20 minutes.
Add the cheese triangles and blend until smooth.
Top and tail the beans and cut them into pieces. Peel and chop the potatoes.
Boil everything in salted water for 20 minutes and drain.
Brown the sliced garlic in the oil, take off the heat and add the paprika.
Pour the garlic oil over the beans and potatoes and mix.
Preheat the oven to 200 °C. Halve the aubergines lengthwise, score the flesh and bake for 25 minutes.
Scoop out the flesh with a spoon, leaving a little attached to the skin.
Soften the onion in the oil, add the meat and the chopped flesh with salt, and cook for 10 minutes. Add the tomato.
Fill the aubergines, top with cheese and grill for 10 minutes.
Soak the raisins in warm water for 10 minutes.
Wash the spinach and blanch for 1 minute in boiling water. Drain well.
Brown the sliced garlic and pine nuts in the oil. Add the drained raisins.
Add the spinach and salt and sauté for 2 minutes.
Boil the cauliflower florets in salted water for 10 minutes and drain.
For the béchamel, melt the butter, add the flour and stir for 2 minutes. Pour in the milk little by little, stirring constantly, until it thickens. Salt.
Put the cauliflower in a dish and cover with the béchamel and cheese.
Grill in the oven at 220 °C for 10–15 minutes, until golden.
Boil the eggs for 10 minutes, cool and peel them.
Wash and cut the lettuce, tomato and onion.
Put everything on a platter with the drained tuna, the quartered eggs and the olives.
Dress with oil, vinegar and salt just before serving.
Wash and chop the tomatoes, the pepper and the peeled cucumber.
Put everything in the blender with the garlic, bread, water, vinegar and salt.
Blend well and add the oil little by little while blending.
Strain it if you want it very smooth, adjust the salt and vinegar and chill for at least 1 hour.
Boil the eggs for 10 minutes and chop them.
Blend the tomatoes and strain the purée.
Add the bread in pieces and the garlic, let the bread soak for 10 minutes and blend again.
Add the oil little by little while blending until thick and creamy. Salt.
Serve cold with the chopped egg and ham on top.
Clean the artichokes, removing the tough leaves and tips, cut into quarters and put them in water with lemon so they don’t darken.
Boil them in salted water for 15–20 minutes and drain, keeping a glass of the water.
Brown the sliced garlic and the diced ham in the oil.
Add the flour, stir, pour in the reserved water and add the artichokes. Cook for 5 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 200 °C.
Put the whole vegetables on a tray, rub with a little oil and roast for 45–50 minutes, turning halfway.
Put them in a covered container for 10 minutes so they sweat and are easy to peel.
Peel them, cut into strips and dress with oil and salt. Serve with the anchovies on top.
Cut all the vegetables into strips or small pieces of the same size.
Heat the wok or a large frying pan with the oil until very hot.
First stir-fry the carrot and broccoli for 3 minutes; then the pepper, courgette, mushrooms and garlic for 3 more minutes, stirring all the time.
Add the soy sauce, stir-fry for 1 minute and serve straight away.
Slice the white part of the leeks and the onion, and soften them in the butter for 10 minutes without browning.
Add the potatoes in chunks and the stock, and cook for 25 minutes.
Blend, add the cream and blend again.
Serve cold or hot.
Slice the courgette, aubergine and onion, and cut the peppers into strips.
Heat the griddle well and brush it with oil.
Cook the vegetables in batches, 3–4 minutes on each side, starting with the firmest.
Serve with coarse salt and a drizzle of oil.
Cut the broccoli into florets and boil for 3 minutes in salted water. Drain.
Brown the sliced garlic and the almonds in the oil.
Add the broccoli and stir-fry for 3–4 minutes over high heat. Salt and serve.
Peel and chop all the vegetables.
Put the oil in a pot and sweat the leek for 5 minutes.
Add the rest of the vegetables, cover with water, salt and cook for 25 minutes.
Blend with some of the cooking liquid until it has the texture you like.
Chop the onion, pepper and garlic and soften them in the oil in a pot for 10 minutes.
Add the paprika, stir for a few seconds and add the rinsed lentils, the carrot, the sliced chorizo and the bay leaf.
Cover with cold water (about 1.5 l) and simmer for 30 minutes.
Add the chopped potatoes and salt, and cook for 20 more minutes until everything is tender.
Fry the bread and 2 garlic cloves in the oil until golden. Crush them with the paprika, cumin, vinegar and a little water.
In the same oil sauté the other garlic clove and the spinach until wilted.
Add the drained chickpeas, the crushed mixture and a glass of water.
Cook for 10 minutes over low heat and season with salt.
The night before, soak the chickpeas in warm salted water.
Put the meats (except the chorizo and black pudding), the pork fat and the bone in a large pot with cold water. When it boils, skim off the foam and add the chickpeas in a mesh bag.
Simmer for 2½ hours (or 40 minutes in a pressure cooker). In the last half hour add the carrots and potatoes.
Cook the chorizo and black pudding separately, and the cabbage too; sauté the cabbage with garlic and oil.
Strain the broth and cook the noodles in it for the soup. Serve the soup first and then the chickpeas, vegetables and meats.
The night before, soak the beans in cold water, and the pork shoulder in another bowl.
Put the beans in a pot with the pork shoulder, pork belly, chorizo and black pudding, and cover with cold water.
Bring to the boil, skim off the foam and «scare» the beans with a splash of cold water two or three times.
Add the saffron and simmer very gently for 2½ hours without stirring (shake the pot) until tender. Salt at the end.
Soak the beans the night before.
Cook them in cold water with half the leek and one carrot, over low heat for 1 hour, «scaring» them with cold water when they boil.
Meanwhile, soften the chopped onion, pepper, garlic and the rest of the leek and carrot in the oil. Add the paprika.
Add the sofrito to the beans, salt and cook for 20 more minutes until tender.
Soak the chickpeas the night before.
Cook them with the bay leaf in hot water for 2 hours (or 30 minutes in a pressure cooker).
Soften the onion and garlic in the oil, add the paprika and add it to the pot with the spinach.
Add the flaked cod and cook for 10 minutes.
Serve with chopped hard-boiled egg on top.
Boil the eggs for 10 minutes and chop them.
Rinse and drain the chickpeas.
Dice the tomato, pepper and onion small.
Mix everything with the tuna and dress with oil, vinegar and salt.
Blend the drained chickpeas with the tahini, lemon juice, garlic, cumin, salt and a little water until creamy.
Put it in a bowl and drizzle with the oil.
Cut the carrots and cucumber into sticks.
Serve with the vegetables and toasted pitta bread.
Soften the chopped onion, pepper and garlic in the oil for 10 minutes. Add the paprika.
Add the rinsed lentils, the bay leaf and 1.5 l of water. Cook for 25 minutes.
Add the rice and salt, and cook for 15–18 more minutes, until the rice is done.
Let it rest for 5 minutes before serving.
Soak the beans the night before.
Cook them in cold water with half an onion, over low heat, «scaring» them with cold water three times.
Meanwhile, fry the rest of the onion, the pepper and the garlic, chopped, in the oil.
After an hour, add the sofrito and the sliced chorizo, salt and cook for 40 more minutes until tender.
Rinse and drain the lentils.
Dice the tomato, pepper, onion and cucumber small.
Mix everything and dress with oil, vinegar and salt.
Leave it in the fridge for 15 minutes before serving.
In the paella pan, brown the salted chicken in the oil. Add the squid rings and the chopped beans and stir for 5 minutes.
Add the chopped garlic and the grated tomato and fry for 5 minutes. Add the paprika.
Add the rice, stir for 1 minute and pour in the hot stock with the saffron. Taste for salt.
Cook for 10 minutes over high heat and 8 over low heat, without stirring. In the last minutes add the prawns and mussels.
Let it rest for 5 minutes covered with a cloth before serving.
Boil the rice in salted water for 18 minutes. Drain and sauté it with a little oil and the garlic.
Heat the tomato sauce.
Fry the plantains, halved lengthwise, and then the eggs.
Serve the rice with the tomato, the egg and the plantain.
Chop the onion and garlic and soften them in the oil in the paella pan for 10 minutes.
Add the chopped squid and grated tomato, and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the rice, stir and pour in the hot stock with the ink dissolved in it. Taste for salt.
Cook for 18 minutes without stirring (10 over high heat and 8 over low heat) and let it rest for 5 minutes. Great with aioli.
Preheat the oven to 220 °C.
Brown the chopped ribs, the sliced potatoes, one sliced tomato and the garlic in the oil. Take them out.
In the same oil fry the other tomato, grated, and the paprika, add the rice and stir.
Transfer everything to a clay dish and arrange the ribs, black pudding in pieces, potatoes, tomato, chickpeas and garlic on top.
Cover with the boiling stock, salt and bake for 20 minutes. Let it rest for 5 minutes.
Toast the noodles in the oil in the paella pan, stirring, until golden. Take them out.
Sauté the prawns and set aside. Fry the chopped squid, chopped garlic and grated tomato for 5 minutes.
Add the paprika, the noodles and the hot stock with the saffron. Taste for salt.
Cook for 10 minutes over medium heat. Put the prawns on top and, if you like, grill for 2 minutes so the noodles curl up.
Cook the macaroni in salted water for the time on the packet and drain.
Soften the chopped onion in the oil, add the diced chorizo and the meat, and cook until browned.
Add the tomato sauce and cook for 5 minutes.
Mix with the macaroni, cover with cheese and grill for 10 minutes in the oven at 220 °C.
Cook the spaghetti in salted water. Keep a glass of the cooking water.
Brown the bacon strips in a pan without oil.
Beat the eggs with the grated parmesan and plenty of pepper.
Drain the pasta and add it to the pan with the bacon, off the heat. Add the egg mixture and a little cooking water and stir quickly so it turns creamy without scrambling.
Cook the sheets as on the packet (or use no-precook sheets).
Soften the onion in the oil, add the diced courgette and aubergine and cook for 15 minutes. Add the spinach and tomato and cook for 10 more minutes.
Make the béchamel: melt the butter, add the flour, stir for 2 minutes and pour in the milk little by little until it thickens. Salt.
In a dish, alternate layers of pasta, vegetables and béchamel. Finish with béchamel and cheese.
Bake at 200 °C for 25 minutes.
Cook the sheets as on the packet and spread them on a cloth.
Soften the onion in the oil, add the meat and salt, and cook for 10 minutes. Mix with the tomato sauce.
Make the béchamel with the butter, flour and milk, and salt it. Add a little to the filling.
Fill and roll the sheets, place them in a dish and cover with the rest of the béchamel and the cheese.
Bake at 200 °C for 20 minutes, until golden.
Keep the stock hot in a saucepan.
Soften the chopped onion in the oil. Add the chopped mushrooms and sauté for 5 minutes.
Add the rice, stir for 1 minute and add the wine.
Add the stock ladle by ladle, stirring, for 18 minutes.
Turn off the heat, add the butter and parmesan, stir and let it rest for 2 minutes.
Cook the pasta in salted water, drain and cool under the tap.
Boil the eggs for 10 minutes and chop them.
Halve the tomatoes.
Mix everything with the tuna, sweetcorn and olives, and dress with oil, vinegar and salt.
Brown the sliced garlic in the oil, add the tomato, sugar and salt, and cook for 15 minutes.
Cook the gnocchi in salted water: they are ready when they float to the surface.
Drain and mix them with the sauce and the torn basil.
Serve with grated parmesan.
Cut all the vegetables into small dice.
Soften the onion and carrot in the oil for 8 minutes. Add the pepper and courgette and cook for 8 more minutes. Add the chickpeas and cumin.
Heat the stock, pour it over the couscous in a bowl, cover and leave for 5 minutes.
Fluff the couscous with a fork and mix it with the vegetables.
Fry the pepper strips, the chopped beans and the quartered artichokes in the oil for 8 minutes.
Add the grated tomato and paprika and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the rice, stir and pour in the hot stock with the saffron and the peas. Taste for salt.
Cook for 18 minutes without stirring and let it rest for 5 minutes.
Peel the potatoes, slice them thinly and slice the onion. Salt.
Cook them gently over medium heat in plenty of oil for about 20 minutes, until tender. Drain well.
Beat the eggs with salt and mix with the potatoes. Let it rest for 5 minutes.
Set the mixture in a pan with a few drops of oil over medium heat for 3–4 minutes. Flip it with a plate and cook for 2 more minutes.
Cut the potatoes into sticks or slices and fry until golden. Salt them.
Fry the eggs in very hot oil, leaving the yolk runny.
Put the potatoes on a platter, the eggs on top and the ham.
Break the eggs over the potatoes just before eating.
Clean the mushrooms and chop them.
Brown the sliced garlic in the oil, add the mushrooms and sauté for 5 minutes. Salt.
Lower the heat, add the eggs beaten with salt and stir gently until set but still juicy.
Finish with chopped parsley.
Make the salad with the lettuce and tomato and dress it with oil, vinegar and salt.
Beat 2 eggs per person with a pinch of salt.
Cook each omelette in a small pan with a few drops of oil, folding it while still soft inside.
Serve with the salad.
Preheat the oven to 200 °C.
Soften the onion in the oil, add the diced chorizo and ham and the peas, and cook for 5 minutes. Add the tomato.
Divide the sauce between small clay dishes and crack two eggs into each.
Bake for 8–10 minutes, until the white sets and the yolk is still runny.
Dice the courgette and slice the onion thinly.
Soften the onion in the oil for 8 minutes and add the courgette. Cook for 10 more minutes, until tender. Salt.
Beat the eggs with salt and mix with the drained vegetables.
Cook the omelette on both sides in a pan with a few drops of oil.
Boil the eggs for 10 minutes, cool in cold water and peel.
Halve them lengthwise and take out the yolks.
Mix half the yolks with the tuna, the chopped olives and half the mayonnaise.
Fill the whites, cover with the rest of the mayonnaise and grate the leftover yolks on top.
Soften the chopped onion, pepper and garlic in the oil for 10 minutes.
Add the cumin, paprika, tomato and salt, and cook for 10 minutes until thick.
Make hollows in the sauce and crack the eggs into them.
Cover and cook over low heat for 6–8 minutes, until the whites set. Serve with parsley and bread for dipping.
Snap off the tough ends of the asparagus and cut into pieces.
Sauté them in the oil with the sliced garlic for 5–6 minutes. Salt.
Add the eggs beaten with salt and stir over low heat until set but still juicy.
Preheat the oven to 180 °C.
Soften the diced onion, pepper and courgette in the oil for 12 minutes, in an ovenproof pan.
Beat the eggs with the cheese and salt and pour over the vegetables.
Cook for 3 minutes on the hob and finish for 10 minutes in the oven.
Preheat the oven to 250 °C (or as hot as it goes).
Roll out the dough on baking paper on a tray.
Spread the tomato and scatter the mozzarella, ham and sliced mushrooms.
Drizzle with the oil, sprinkle oregano and bake for 10–12 minutes, until the edges are golden.
Melt the butter, add the chopped ham and the flour and stir for 3 minutes.
Pour in the hot milk little by little, stirring constantly, for about 15 minutes, until you have a thick dough that comes away from the pan. Taste for salt.
Spread it in a dish, cover with cling film touching the surface and chill in the fridge for at least 4 hours.
Shape the croquettes and coat them in beaten egg and breadcrumbs.
Fry in plenty of very hot oil, a few at a time, until golden.
Preheat the oven to 190 °C. Boil one egg for 10 minutes.
Soften the onion and the pepper in strips in the oil for 20 minutes. Add the tomato, the flaked tuna and the chopped hard-boiled egg.
Lay one sheet of dough on the tray, spread the cold filling and cover with the other sheet. Seal the edges.
Make a hole in the middle, brush with the other beaten egg and bake for 35–40 minutes.
Whisk the flour, eggs, milk, melted butter and a pinch of salt until smooth. Let it rest for 15 minutes.
Heat a non-stick pan with a dab of butter and pour in a small ladle of batter, tilting the pan to cover the base.
When it comes away, flip it and cook for 30 more seconds.
Fill each crêpe with ham and cheese, fold and heat for 1 minute so the cheese melts.
Boil the eggs for 10 minutes and chop them.
Heat the stock and, when it boils, add the noodles. Cook for 5 minutes.
Add the chopped ham and egg.
Serve with a few mint leaves.
Soften the chopped onion, pepper and garlic in the oil for 10 minutes.
Add the sliced chorizo and stir for 2 minutes. Add the paprika.
Add the «cracked» potatoes (breaking off the last cut), stir and cover with water. Add the bay leaf and salt.
Simmer for 25–30 minutes, until the potatoes are tender and the broth thickens.
Slice the onions very thinly and cook them slowly in the butter for 30 minutes, until golden.
Add the flour, stir and pour in the wine. Let it reduce.
Add the stock and cook for 15 minutes. Taste for salt.
Divide into ovenproof bowls, top with the toasted bread and the cheese, and grill until golden.
Toast the bread.
Grate the tomatoes and season with oil and salt.
Spread some toasts with tomato and add ham; others with cheese; and others with avocado mashed with salt.
Finish with a drizzle of oil.
Preheat the oven to 190 °C. Line a tin with the pastry, prick it with a fork and bake for 10 minutes.
Soften the leek in the oil for 8 minutes and add the spinach until wilted.
Beat the eggs with the cream, cheese and salt, and mix with the vegetables.
Pour the filling onto the pastry and bake for 30 minutes, until set.
Peel the potatoes and cut into sticks. Rinse and dry them well.
Fry them in plenty of oil over medium heat for 10 minutes, then raise the heat for 2–3 minutes to brown them. Drain and salt.
Pass the ham strips through that oil for a few seconds, or leave them raw, to taste.
Fry the eggs one at a time in very hot oil, spooning oil over them so the white gets crispy edges and the yolk stays runny.
Serve two eggs per person with the chips and ham.
If the lobster is alive, put it in the freezer for 15 minutes to send it to sleep.
Split it in half lengthwise with a large knife and crack the claws a little.
Chop the garlic and parsley and mix with the oil.
Put the lobsters flesh side down on a very hot griddle for 4–5 minutes. Turn them, brush with the garlic and parsley oil and cook for 4–5 more minutes. The claws need 8–10 minutes.
Serve with coarse salt and lemon.
Keep the caviar in the fridge until the last moment and serve it on ice, with a spoon that isn’t metal (mother-of-pearl, bone or plastic).
Toast the bread, remove the crusts and cut into small triangles.
Boil the eggs for 10 minutes, cool and chop the white and yolk separately. Chop the onion very finely.
Serve the caviar in its tin with the toasts, cream, egg, onion and lemon, so everyone can make their own.
Spread one side of each slice with a little butter.
Build the sandwiches with the butter on the outside: ham, cheese and a few thin slices of tomato.
Toast them in a pan over medium heat for 2–3 minutes on each side, pressing lightly, until the cheese melts.
